Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Hexaconazole, EC is used against fungal diseases of the various agricultural crops. 

The product has been registered for production and use in the country under the provisions of Insecticides Act, 
1968 and Rules framed thereunder. In preparation of this standard, due consideration has, therefore, been given 
to the provisions of the Act and the Rules framed thereunder as well as the Standards of Weights and Measures 
(Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these 
wherever appUcable. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a pardcular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values {revisedy. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 14550 : 1998 



Indian Standard 
HEXACONAZOLE, EC — SPECMCATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes the requirements and 
methods of sampling and test for hexaconazole, EC. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provision of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to agreements based on 
this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated below:

3.2.3 Flash Point (Abel) 

When tested by the method prescribed in IS 1448 
[P : 2], the flash point of the material shall be above 

24.5C. 

3.2.4 Emulsion Stability 

Any separation including creaming at the top and 
sedimentation at the bottom of 100 ml emulsion 
nrgnar^d lu staudafd hard water with 2.0 ml 
concentrate shall not exceed 2.0 ml when tested by the 
method prescribed in 13.3 of IS 6940. 

3.3 Chemical 

The material shall comply with the chemical 
requirements specified in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2, 

3.3,1 Hexaconazole Content 

The nominal hexaconazole content shall be declared 
[see 5 A (g)]. When tested by the method prescribed in 
Annex A of IS 14549, the observed hexaconazole 
content percent (m/m) shall not differ from the 
declared nominal value by more than the percent 
tolerance limits indicated below (see also 6.1). 



3 REQUIREMENT 

3.1 Constituents 

3.1.1 The material shall consist of hexaconazole, 
technical conforming to IS 14549, dissolved in 
suitable solvent(s) together with emulsifier(s). 

3.2 Physical 

The material shall comply with the physical 
requirements specified in 3.2.1 to 3.2.4. 

3.2.1 Description 

The material shall be a clear, stable, homogeneous 
liquid. It shall be free from sediments and/or 
suspended matter. On dilution with water, it shall 
readily form an emulsion, suitable for use as spray, 

3.2.2 Cold Test 

When tested by the method prescribed in 13.1 of 
IS 6940, no turbidity or separation of solid and/or oily 
matter shall occur.

When tested by the method prescribed in 13.5 of 
IS 6940, the acidity (as H2SO4) or alkalinity 
(as NaOH) shall not be more than 0.5 percent by mass. 



The material shall be packed in lacquered tinplate or 
aluminium containers. It shall also conform to the 
general requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 2). 

5 MARKING 

5.1 The container shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the following information: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number or code number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry;

5.2 BIS Certification Marking 

The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 

5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 



The details of conditions under which the licence for 
the use of Standard Mark may be grsintod to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 

6 SAMPLING 

When bulk manufactured material is offered for 
inspection, representative samples of the material shall 
be drawn as prescribed in IS 10627 and tested within 
90 days of its manufacture. The criteria for conformity 
shall be as given in IS 10627. When the material is 
o;ffered for inspection after 90 days of its manufacture,
